text:
riley: Heads-up — I’m seeing request-scoped KV entries from session A getting served to later sessions after long-context runs. Posting quick logs + repro.

riley: Repro (super short):
1) start long generation (~40k tokens) with streaming on binding X
2) immediately send a short follow-up request on same worker
3) follow-up returns prefixes that look like the end of the long run (wrong user tokens)

riley: Example log snippet from the worker:
```
[KV] page_id=42 slot=5 session_tag=0x7f3a req_id=abc123 start_tok=40960 len=128
[KV] append -> stored at page=42 offset=40960
[KV] evict partial page=42 keep=40960..41152 session_tag=0x7f3a
[KV] serve request req_id=def456 -> served block from page=42 offset=40960 session_tag=0x7f3a
```

maya: whoa. can repro on my laptop with the e2e harness in ~2 runs. short repro script incoming.

jon: I ran perf + heap profile during the repro. Observations:
- kv-resident memory creeps linearly after repeated long runs (+~60MB / long session)
- got stale entries referenced by new request ids in the trace logs
- timeline shows partial-evict then immediate re-attach of same page to next request

jon: Perf excerpt (top lines):
```
KV: live_fragments=312 -> 378
KV: total_bytes=1.22GB -> 1.55GB
runtime: cpu p95 spike during append/evict
``` 

kevin: suspect alignment logic in page-split + reuse path. If we split and only zero some metadata, session_tag might remain and cause a subsequent `is_owned_by_session()` check to pass incorrectly.

riley: I looked at the code. The fast-path on append does `if (page->session_tag == current_session) { reuse_slot(...) }` but on partial-evict we do `memmove` and forget to clear `page->session_tag` when the kept range no longer belongs to that session (race if the last write hasn't completed).

riley: Pseudocode that feels wrong:
```
void partial_evict(page, keep_start, keep_len) {
  // copy kept bytes to front
  memmove(page->buf, page->buf + keep_start, keep_len);
  page->len = keep_len;
  // BUG: we don't clear page->session_tag when keep_len < original_len
}
```

maya: I can reproduce a failing assertion if I add a check `assert(page->session_tag == 0 || page->owner_req == current)` — fails in the short request path.

jon: Also saw a case where token alignment is off by 8 tokens after a split (likely integer rounding of shard offsets). That explains garbled token slicing.

kevin: Quick mitigation idea: on partial evict, clear session_tag and set a `generation++` marker so any concurrent lookup fails safe and forces re-fetch. Cheap and safe.

riley: I'll open a hotfix PR to zero session_tag on eviction + add a unit test for split+reuse scenario. PR will be small: clearing the tag + a test that simulates interleaved requests.

riley: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4823 (draft) — includes reproducer harness and heap assertion

infra-bot: canary deploy queued for runtime:v2026.03. Will run 3 canaries across us-west2.

kevin: nice. also add a telemetry gauge to track `kv_session_tag_leaks` so we can alert if nonzero after eviction.

maya: I’ll run the harness overnight against the canary and report back in the morning. If stable, we can push to prod.

riley: thx team. CC @kevin for triage, @jon for profile follow-up. I’ll post follow-up logs here when the canary finishes.
